name: fee-ids-for-merchant-period
pattern: (applicable fee ids for <merchant>|fee ids applicable to <merchant>)
operation: the fee rules whose criteria match a merchant's transactions in a day, month or year
invariant: ids(day) ⊆ ids(month) ⊆ ids(year) for one merchant

guidelines.guideline: Answer must be a list of values in comma separated list, eg: A, B, C. If the answer is an empty list, reply with an empty string. If a question does not have a relevant or applicable answer for the task, please respond with 'Not Applicable'

canonical_method.helper: applicable_fee_ids(fees, transactions, account_type, mcc, capture_delay, monthly_fraud_level, monthly_volume)
steps: cd_bucket = capture_delay_bucket(info['capture_delay'])  — MANDATORY, never pass the raw capture_delay string
for each calendar month touching the period: stats = monthly_merchant_stats(payments, merchant, year, month)

call applicable_fee_ids(fees, transactions=<period-filtered txns>, account_type=info['account_type'], mcc=info['merchant_category_code'], capture_delay=cd_bucket, monthly_fraud_level=stats['monthly_fraud_level_bucket'], monthly_volume=stats['monthly_volume_bucket'])
day/month answers: transactions = that day's/month's rows only, but the fraud/volume bucket still comes from the containing natural month's monthly_merchant_stats
year answer: union the id sets returned per month

conflict_ruling: task 1709 (day-level, PASS-worthy: calls capture_delay_bucket() then applicable_fee_ids()) is right. task 1808 (month-level) hardcoded capture_delay='7' instead of bucketing it, which is why ids 17/427/634 are present in the day answer but silently absent from the month/year answers — that is the root cause of the two FAILED subset-invariant checks, not a data issue.
pitfalls: Passing merchant_info['capture_delay'] raw (e.g. '7') instead of capture_delay_bucket(...) silently drops fee rules that key on the bucket string (e.g. '>5'), breaking ids(day)⊆ids(month)⊆ids(year)
Hand-rolling the wildcard-match loop instead of applicable_fee_ids/fee_rule_matches (task 1745) risks missing the null/[]-means-everything rule on scalar fields
Year-level answers must union per-month id sets, not run applicable_fee_ids once with a single annual fraud/volume bucket
applicable_fee_ids takes fees/transactions positionally plus keyword-only merchant filters — no 'merchant='/'year='/'month=' kwargs (task 1773's first attempt)

few_shot.question: For the 300th of the year 2023, what are the Fee IDs applicable to Rafa_AI?

prompt_rule: if the question asks for applicable/fee IDs for a merchant over a day/month/year → get_merchant_info + capture_delay_bucket + monthly_merchant_stats (per month) + applicable_fee_ids, union across months for year; answer format: comma-separated sorted ids, empty string if none, 'Not Applicable' only if the merchant/period has no defined concept.
note: 45 tasks, largest family alongside F03/F08 — the capture_delay_bucket omission bug likely recurs in F03/F05/F09/F10 wherever the same fee-matching preamble is needed.
